name: MonarchTreeView
title: TreeView
summary: A hierarchy people can browse and pick from, such as departments, goals and key results or a document outline, drawn as indented rows in a lazy list.
whenToUse: For nested data of unknown depth where people open branches and pick one or more items: an org chart, a folder tree, an outline.
whenNotToUse: For one level of sections that open and close, use MonarchCollapsible or an accordion. For two levels, a list with section headers is easier to scan. For moving between screens, use navigation.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTreeView(items: List<MonarchTreeViewItem>, expanded: Set<String>, onExpandedChange: (Set<String>) -> Unit, expandIcon: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, selectionMode: MonarchTreeViewSelectionMode = MonarchTreeViewSelectionMode.Single, selected: Set<String> = emptySet(), current: String? = null, loading: Set<String> = emptySet(), state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), onSelectedChange: ((Set<String>) -> Unit)? = null, onActivate: ((MonarchTreeViewItem) -> Unit)? = null, onLoadChildren: ((MonarchTreeViewItem) -> Unit)? = null, icon: (@Composable (MonarchTreeViewItem) -> Unit)? = null, meta: (@Composable (MonarchTreeViewItem) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchTreeViewLabels = MonarchTreeViewLabels())

class MonarchTreeViewItem(id: String, label: String, description: String? = null, children: List<MonarchTreeViewItem>? = null, hasChildren: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true) { val isParent: Boolean }
enum class MonarchTreeViewSelectionMode { None, Single, Multiple }

class MonarchTreeViewLabels(expand: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, collapse: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, expanded: String? = null, collapsed: String? = null, level: ((level: Int) -> String)? = null, loading: String? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The top-level items.

options.name: expanded
options.description: The ids of the open parents.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called with the new set when the user opens or closes a parent.

options.name: expandIcon
options.description: A chevron that points to the end, mirrored in right to left; it turns a quarter turn while open. Required because Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the list. Give it a bounded height or let it fill a screen.

options.name: selectionMode
options.description: None (navigation only; a tap on a parent opens it), Single or Multiple.

options.name: selected
options.description: The ids of the selected items.

options.name: current
options.description: The id of the item that matches the current screen or position; drawn in semibold strong accent text.

options.name: loading
options.description: The ids of the parents whose children are loading; each shows a "Loading" row.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the list.

options.name: onSelectedChange
options.description: Called with the new selection when the user taps an item.

options.name: onActivate
options.description: Called when the user taps an item: open the record, scroll to the heading.

options.name: onLoadChildren
options.description: Called when the user opens an item with hasChildren and no children; add its id to loading, then give the children or close it.

options.name: icon
options.description: A decorative icon before the label of an item.

options.name: meta
options.description: Content at the end of a row that is not an action, such as a MonarchBadge or a count.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings monarch_treeview_*.

options.name: MonarchTreeViewItem.id
options.description: A stable id, unique in the whole tree.

options.name: MonarchTreeViewItem.label
options.description: The visible name.

options.name: MonarchTreeViewItem.description
options.description: A second line under the label.

options.name: MonarchTreeViewItem.children
options.description: The children; an empty list is a parent with no children, null a leaf unless hasChildren.

options.name: MonarchTreeViewItem.hasChildren
options.description: The item has children that are not loaded yet.

options.name: MonarchTreeViewItem.enabled
options.description: false makes the item impossible to select, activate or open.

states.name: collapsed parent
states.description: The expand icon points to the end; the row reads "Collapsed, Level 1".

states.name: expanded parent
states.description: The icon turns a quarter turn and the children follow, indented by one level.

states.name: selected
states.description: The subtle accent fill, a solid accent bar at the start, semibold strong accent text and the selected state.

states.name: loading
states.description: A row with a small progress ring and "Loading" under the parent; the ring is left out when animations are off.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Disabled text; the row and its expand button ignore taps.

appearance: Rows are at least 48dp tall with small rounded corners, indented 20dp per level. Labels are body text in the default text color, descriptions muted caption text, the expand icon muted. The selected row has the subtle accent fill with strong accent text and a solid accent bar at its start edge. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web TreeView implements the WAI-ARIA tree pattern by hand: roving focus, arrow keys, typeahead, single or multiple selection, aria-current, lazy children and row actions. Compose has no tree, so Monarch builds one on a LazyColumn (iOS uses the system List with children instead). Expansion and selection are hoisted; the web's uncontrolled defaultExpanded and defaultSelected are not offered. Lazy children are asked for with onLoadChildren and shown loading through the loading set, where the web awaits a promise; a failed load is the app's to show, for example with MonarchInlineErrorRetry, and to close. With a hardware keyboard the arrow keys towards the end and the start open and close a parent; typeahead, Home and End and the select-all shortcut are not offered, and focus moves with the system's directional focus. The outline variant with indentation guides and the renderActions slot are not offered: put row actions in the screen's top bar or a menu on the selected item. Android has no tree role, so the level is part of the state TalkBack reads. The parity map lists collapsible and checkbox: rows open with their own expand button rather than MonarchCollapsible, because a tree row holds no content of its own, and multiple selection uses the selected state and the start bar rather than a checkbox per row.
accessibility: Each row is one TalkBack element: the label and description, then the state, "Expanded, Level 1", "Collapsed, Level 1" or "Level 2".
Parents offer the TalkBack expand and collapse actions on the row.
The expand icon is a separate button named "Expand Engineering" or "Collapse Engineering", with a 48dp touch target reserved in the layout.
With selection, rows expose the selected state; without selection, rows have the button role.
Selection is shown by the start bar and semibold text as well as the color.
Disabled items are announced as disabled and ignore taps.
The "Loading" row is a polite live region.
Labels wrap at the largest font size instead of being cut off.
edgeCases: A parent with an empty children list opens to nothing.
Expanding an item with hasChildren and no children calls onLoadChildren once per opening; keep the id in loading until the children arrive.
Deep trees indent 20dp per level; past five or six levels at 320dp wide the labels get narrow.
The tree is a lazy list: it cannot sit inside another vertical scroll without a bounded height.
